already_extracted_claims: The source says CRO should increase a specific metric and recommends tracking a mix of conversion rate and average order value, focusing nine times out of ten on revenue per visitor or revenue per session.
The source says in 2025, brands under 300,000 sessions per month are far better taking much bigger swings.
The source says brands over 300,000 sessions per month with good enough conversion rate and enough orders have enough data to quantify comprehensive full CRO.
The source says driving media straight to PDPs, product pages, homepages, or collection pages leaves money on the table.
The source says if brands are not using LPS, listicles, sales pages, advertorials, or different angles, they are leaving money on the table, and emphasizes trying different angles.
The source says under 300,000 sessions, brands should no longer test small PDP elements like button color, above-fold image, or small text snippet, and should do PDP redesigns based on data.
The source says offer testing and price testing are things that move the needle.
The source recommends free shipping and price testing within cart and checkout, and boosting average order value with free shipping prompts and cart gamification.
The source recommends post-purchase upsells and surveys using Zipify and says it is a great way of doing these things.
The source says if creative does not speak to the landing page, the brand is losing money.
Comprehensive CRO includes comprehensive audits with deep qualitative and quantitative research.
Comprehensive CRO includes isolated AB tests with incremental increases in revenue per visitor.

The source says a high experiment velocity means doing four to eight AB tests per month because there is enough data; without enough data, there are not enough people to quantify winning or losing tests.
Comprehensive CRO includes a full data stack with G4 analysis, heat map analysis, survey analysis, session recordings, and full road maps and frameworks.
The source recommends learning from wins, taking more time to see why tests lose, and implementing changes in winning and future tests.
The source includes cross-functional teamwork as part of comprehensive CRO.
The source says he could guarantee improving conversion rates in about two minutes by slashing prices, but if prices are halved, conversion rate shoots up while the brand makes less per visitor.
The source says driving paid media to a store without CRO is throwing money into a leaky bucket, while optimizing the store with CRO gains that revenue and increases revenue per person.

The speaker personally believes nothing is more powerful than conversion rate optimization for moving the profitability of a store user in ecommerce, and says to forget paid media, email, and retention.
The source gives an example where an unoptimized site has revenue per click of $120 and an optimized site produces $380 per person without increasing ad spend.

The source says that when cost per click is high and conversion rate does not increase much, focusing on optimizing the site with bigger swings can literally double conversion or revenue per session overnight.
The source says the CRO and AB testing landscape has changed in the last six to twelve months because of external factors such as tracking changes and increasing CPMs, making attribution harder.
The source says comprehensive CRO still works and is still the most powerful thing a brand over 300,000 sessions can do to generate more revenue per visitor.
The source says a step should be put between post-click and the store landing, specifically a landing page where people are pre-sold before going to product or collection pages.
The source defines a listicle as content like 'top five reasons why people are loving this new supplement'.
The source defines an advertorial as a content piece written in first or third party perspective that reviews a product while pre-educating people through content.

The source says brands should test different offers on a month-to-month basis, including buy one get one free, three for the power of two, build-a-bundle pages, different price points, and price testing.
The source recommends testing a tool called Intelligence, which sponsors its conversion rate conference, or working with the speaker's team to run price testing.
The source cites Ezra saying his brand just created three new landing pages, and says landing pages will work even though his brand is bigger than the under-300,000-session threshold.
The source says brands need to be testing listicles and advertorials.
